result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.describe()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Print a comprehensive description of the graph. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L1361-L1512){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.describe(describe_hook=None) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Displays key graph properties including node/edge counts, connectivity, degree statistics, and optional custom properties via a hook function. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [describe_hook]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[callable]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : A function that takes a Graph as input and returns a dictionary of additional properties to include. Keys are property names, values are the corresponding values to display. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} The `describe_hook=` parameter allows you to compute expensive metrics only when needed. For large graphs, computing properties like diameter or clustering can be slow. ## Examples {.doc-examples} Calling `describe()` prints a structured summary straight to the console -- node and edge counts, density, degree statistics, and connectivity, tailored to whether the graph is directed or undirected: ::: {#4783b75f .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_edge("A", "B") .add_edge("B", "C") ) graph.describe() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Number of nodes : 3 Number of edges : 2 Directed : False Density : 0.67 Average degree (min, max) : 1.33 (1, 2) Connected : True Number of connected components : 1 Tree : True Bipartite : True ``` ::: ::: Pass `describe_hook=` to append your own computed properties to the printout -- useful for metrics that are too expensive to compute automatically on every call: ::: {#bdea8726 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.karate_club() def custom_stats(g): return { "Clustering": g.get_avg_clustering_coefficient(), "Diameter": g.get_diameter() or "N/A" } graph.describe(describe_hook=custom_stats) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Name of Graph : Zachary's Karate Club Number of nodes : 34 Number of edges : 78 Directed : False Density : 0.14 Average degree (min, max) : 4.59 (1, 17) Connected : True Number of connected components : 1 Tree : False Bipartite : False Clustering : 0.5706384782076823 Diameter : 5 ``` ::: ::: On a larger, real-world graph the same call surfaces its overall shape at a glance -- here, the well-known Zachary's karate club network: ::: {#b2d3d759 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec G = ec.karate_club() G.describe() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Name of Graph : Zachary's Karate Club Number of nodes : 34 Number of edges : 78 Directed : False Density : 0.14 Average degree (min, max) : 4.59 (1, 17) Connected : True Number of connected components : 1 Tree : False Bipartite : False ``` ::: :::
